subject: Post-call: reliability & SLO follow-up / next tests vs hyperscaler
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: reliability & SLO follow-up / next tests vs hyperscaler

Great to meet you both today — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- Primary ask: validate Redwood's production reliability compared to your current hyperscaler endpoints (latency under load, failover behavior, rate limiting, and error budgets).
- Success criteria you mentioned: sustained throughput for peak windows, predictable tail latency (p99), and clear behavior on region/zone failover. Procurement also wants an error-budget policy and SLA credit examples.

What we propose as next tests (we can run these in collaboration or provide a dedicated test endpoint):
1) Baseline throughput: 30-minute sustained run at 500 QPS (representative prompt mix) to capture p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization.
2) Spike test: controlled 5-minute ramp to 2k QPS to observe autoscaling and queueing behavior.
3) Failover simulation: terminate a single serving pool / AZ and measure tail latency and successful failover within configured SLO window.
4) Rate-limit & retry behavior: burst traffic (token-heavy requests) to understand throttling, 429 patterns, and our automatic backpressure/retry behavior.

Capabilities / differentiators to call out vs hyperscalers:
- Per-route SLOs and automatic fallback to compatible model variants (keeps app online vs full outage).
- Prefix/KV caching reduces cost and stabilizes latency for repeated user sessions.
- Transparent error budgets and SLA credit policy (we document the math and provide credits for sustained breaches).
- Production-first serving runtime tuned for inference (continuous batching, kernel selection, optimized KV cache).

Ask from Acme: please confirm which tests you'd like Redwood to run vs run from your side, and share a short list of top-3 prompts to emulate real traffic.

I've attached our SLO comparison matrix (redwood-reliability-slo-matrix.xlsx) to give you the initial numbers we expect to show. I can also provide a temporary test key and a runbook for the failover test.

Next steps / timeline:
- Confirm desired tests and approximate test window (we recommend scheduling a 2-hour window for the baseline + spike + failover choreography).
- We can prep a POC DocuSign if procurement needs it; otherwise we can open a short-term eval account.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call to walk through the test plan.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Confirming — I'll own the runbook and loadgen config. Quick notes below for the test plan and what we'll share with Acme: 

- Retries & backoff: we recommend client-side 2 retries with exponential backoff (initial 200ms, multiplier 2x) for idempotent requests. Server-side we have short-lived internal retries for transient GPU preemption but those are bounded to avoid amplifying load.
- Circuit-breaker: our edge enforces token-based quotas per route; sustained 429s trigger a local circuit-breaker after configurable failure thresholds (default: 5 failures / 60s), and the system falls back to a warm model variant when available to preserve availability.
- Error budget example (99.9% monthly uptime): 
  - Monthly minutes = 30 * 24 * 60 = 43,200 minutes
  - Allowed downtime at 99.9% = 43.2 minutes
  - If observed downtime > 43.2 minutes, SLA credit calculation is X% of monthly usage (we'll include the explicit credit table in the SLO matrix).
- Failover choreography: we'll document the exact steps to simulate AZ failure (drain pool, observe traffic shift, validate p99). Expected failover completion: target < 30s for most read-heavy workloads; write-heavy or long-generation sessions may take longer depending on KV warming.

Attachments we'll provide: loadgen-config.json and a short runbook PDF. Also linking a dashboard & the deal record: https://kibana.redwood.internal/d/acme-reliability, https://hubspot.example.com/deal/DEAL-2026-078

I'll have the runbook + loadgen config to you by EOD Thursday so Ben can send the test key Friday.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
